subject: Renewal paperwork: coverage addendum & MSA indemnity language
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-06-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal — updated order form and coverage addendum

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As discussed, attached is our proposed order form for the renewal (ACME_OrderForm_v2.docx) and a brief note on the coverage addendum we'd like to include for the next 12 months. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm the term change from 12 to 18 months and how proration of billing will be handled at mid-term upgrades.
- Add a short carve-out in Section 7 for regulated-data routing restrictions (we've flagged language in the attached).
- We want indemnity language to remain symmetrical; if Redwood has standard suggested language, please share so Legal can compare.

Can you loop in whoever will handle the redlines on your side? We are on a tight timeline for procurement — would like to get final paper signed by 6/24 if possible.

Best,
Elena Rodriguez
VP, Procurement
Acme Health

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v2.docx

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — updated order form and coverage addendum

Elena — thanks for the materials and the clear bullets. I pulled a first-pass from Legal and attached a PDF of our redlines (Evelyn_Redlines_ACME.pdf). A few quick notes:

- Term/proration: we're comfortable with 18 months; for mid-term capacity upgrades we propose prorating at the invoice-cycle level (same approach we used for similar accounts). We'll capture this in the order form.
- Regulated-data routing carve-out: agree to the restriction, but need to confirm how that impacts our routing fallback policy — looped in Dev to advise on technical implications.
- Indemnity: Legal prefers a more limited carve (we'll suggest language that narrows the scope to third-party claims arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct).

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev to confirm whether the routing language is operationally feasible without an SLA exception.
2) Marissa to consolidate the suggested MSA clause and return a clean snippet.
3) If ACME is good with our snippet, we'll prepare an exhibit and send for DocuSign.

Targeting a follow-up doc by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Director
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Evelyn_Redlines_ACME.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — updated order form and coverage addendum

On Thu, Jun 10, 2026 at 4:05 PM, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the materials and the clear bullets. I pulled a first-pass from Legal and attached a PDF of our redlines (Evelyn_Redlines_ACME.pdf).

Hi all — quick internal note and suggested language below (copying ACME since these are proposed edits, not final language).

Overview of proposed adjustments:
- Narrow indemnity: proposed to limit Redwood's indemnity to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct and exclude consequential damages except where required by law.
- Billing/proration clause: add explicit formula for mid-term capacity increases: prorated at daily rate based on upgraded seat/token tier, invoiced on next regular billing cycle.
- Routing/residency: accept ACME's routing restriction but add an exception for emergency failover to a compliant region with prior notice and documented change control.

Suggested indemnity snippet (for Legal to vet):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither Party shall be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, consequential, special, exemplary or punitive damages, except to the extent such damages arise from gross negligence or willful misconduct. Each Party's aggregate liability arising under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer under the applicable Order Form during the twelve (12) month period preceding the claim."

Please review and flag anything ACME cannot accept; if ACME is neutral on the exception language for failover, we can finalize the order form and prepare exhibits.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-06-11T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — updated order form and coverage addendum

Marissa — thanks for the proposed language, that helps a lot. A couple of quick comments from Acme Legal:

- The liability cap tied to 12 months of fees is acceptable, but can you confirm whether fees are calculated on a lookback of the prior 12 months or projected annualized run-rate? Acme prefers lookback if possible.
- The emergency failover exception needs a short SLA: if Redwood initiates failover, ACME requests written notice within 48 hours and a mitigation plan within 10 business days.

I'll attach our security questionnaire (ACME_Security_Questionnaire.pdf) — some of the residency questions are here and may influence the final section language. We'll review the indemnity snippet with contracts@acmehealth.com and circle back.

If you can confirm the fee lookback approach, we can likely proceed to finalize and DocuSign.

Best,
Elena

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena.rodriguez@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal — updated order form and coverage addendum

Elena — quick operational answers from my side:

- Failover / routing: we can implement the residency carve-out with the requested emergency failover, but we need the 48-hour notice + 10 business day mitigation plan in writing to satisfy change control. That aligns with our ops playbook.
- Fee lookback: Redwood's standard is a 12-month lookback (actual fees billed in the prior 12 months). If ACME needs projected run-rate billing for forecasting, we can add an exhibit that shows projected monthly charges, but it will be informational only and not used to set liability caps.

I've pasted a short proposed indemnity/text snippet in the attached file (proposed_indemnity_snippet.txt) that incorporates the lookback definition and the notice/mitigation timeline. If Legal is OK, I'll prepare a clean order-form PDF with the exhibit and route for DocuSign.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Dir, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_indemnity_snippet.txt
